misheberah.title: Mi Sheberach
misheberah.lead: A prayer for the health and well-being of someone close.
misheberah.text: “Mi Sheberach” — “He Who blessed” — is said during the Torah reading on Monday, Thursday and Shabbat. The person is named by their own name and their mother's name; if they have a Hebrew name, it is used. It can be ordered for someone who is ill, travelling, giving birth, or anyone who needs support.

kaddish.title: Kaddish
kaddish.lead: The memorial prayer during the eleven months after the passing of a loved one.
kaddish.text: Kaddish is an Aramaic prayer sanctifying the Name of the Almighty. It is said with a minyan — ten adult men. After the death of a parent it is customary to say Kaddish for eleven months; if the family cannot do it themselves, it is said in the synagogue at their request.

yahrzeit.title: Yahrzeit
yahrzeit.lead: The anniversary of a death by the Jewish calendar.
yahrzeit.text: Yahrzeit is observed every year on the day of death by the Jewish calendar: a memorial candle is lit, Kaddish and “El Male Rachamim” are said, tzedakah is given. From the date of death we will work out the Hebrew date of the anniversary and, if you wish, remind you in advance.

yizkor.title: Yizkor
yizkor.lead: Remembrance of the departed on festivals.
yizkor.text: Yizkor — “May He remember” — is said four times a year: on Yom Kippur, Shemini Atzeret, the last day of Passover and the second day of Shavuot. The names of departed relatives are mentioned and a pledge of tzedakah is made in their memory.
